author: MiamiGent
title: CNBCU.S. stock futures were lower this morning, but
text:
CNBC 

U.S. stock futures were lower this morning, but where the markets end the day may well depend on the latest Fed meeting minutes. The Dow and S&P 500 saw six-day win streaks end Tuesday, with the Dow posting 2018's fifth decline of 1 percent or more. (CNBC) 

* Market sell-offs 'tend to happen in three waves' (CNBC) 

The Fed minutes are out at 2 p.m. ET, with investors focused on gleaning any further insights on inflation. Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari and Philadelphia Fed President Patrick Harker speak today. (CNBC) 

Mortgage interest rates jumped again last week, causing mortgage applications to fall 6.6 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis from the previous week. Refis fell 7 percent. Meanwhile, January existing home sales figures are out at 10 a.m. ET. (CNBC) 

IN THE NEWS TODAY 

President Donald Trump said he has recommended that "bump stocks," devices that let semi-automatic weapons fire hundreds of rounds per minute," be banned. His announcement came six days after a gunman killed 17 people at a high school in Parkland, Florida. (CNBC) 

The final version of a landmark deal aimed at cutting trade barriers in some of the Asia-Pacific's fastest-growing economies was released today, signalling the pact was a step closer to reality even without the U.S. (Reuters) 

The FCC is expected to publish tomorrow its December order overturning the landmark Obama-era net neutrality rule, sources tell Reuters. That means state attorneys and advocacy groups will be able to sue in a bid to block the order. 

* White House considers allowing more Americans to erase student debt (WSJ) 

E-commerce giant Amazon (AMZN) quietly launched an exclusive line of over-the-counter health products that include products ranging from ibuprofen to hair regrowth treatment. The line is a possible challenge to pharmacy retail chains. (CNBC) 

Apple (AAPL) is in talks to buy cobalt supplies for its iPhone batteries directly from miners, according to a Bloomberg report. Cobalt prices have been surging due to increasing demand for the lithium ion batteries used in electric vehicles. 

Tesla's (TSLA) cloud system was hijacked by hackers who used it to mine cryptocurrency, researchers say. Cryptocurrency mining is a process whereby miners solve complex mathematical problems to validate a transaction and add it to the underlying network. (CNBC) 

STOCKS TO WATCH 

JPMorgan (JPM) announced today, in conjunction with New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio, plans to build a new 2.5 million square foot headquarters at its 270 Park Avenue location in New York City. 

General Motors (GM) has proposed a $2.8 billion investment into its South Korean operations over the next decade. The automaker recently announced plans to close one of its four South Korea plants and evaluate the future of the other three. 

Japan will buy at least 20 more of Lockheed Martin's (LMT) F-35A stealth fighters over the next six years, according to sources quoted by Reuters. 

Dish Network's (DISH) fourth-quarter profit surged due to a roughly $1.2 billion benefit related to U.S. tax law reforms. Revenue of 3.48 billion fell short of estimates and nearly 8 percent from a year ago. 

Foot Locker (FL) increased its quarterly dividend by 11 percent, and the athletic apparel and footwear retailer also announced a new $230 million capital expenditure program for 2018. 

LendingClub (LC) reported adjusted quarterly profit of a penny per share, missing the consensus estimate of 2 cents. The online lender also saw revenue come in below estimates amid increased loan origination and servicing expenses. 

Boyd Gaming (BYD) came in 5 cents shy of estimates with adjusted quarterly profit of 22 cents per share, and the casino operator's revenue also came up short of forecasts. That was primarily due to a shortfall in the Las Vegas market.
